query: Which material can be used for enhance glass-forming ability, and why?

generation.hypothesis: The addition of a small amount of yttrium (Y) to a magnesium-based metallic glass alloy will enhance its glass-forming ability by reducing the nucleation rate of crystalline phases during rapid cooling.
generation.intervention: addition of 1-2 at.% yttrium (Y) to the alloy
generation.conditions: rapid cooling at a rate of 10^3 K/s
generation.structural_mediator: reduced nucleation rate of crystalline phases
generation.mechanism: the large atomic size mismatch between Y and Mg atoms hinders the formation of crystalline nuclei, thereby enhancing the glass-forming ability
generation.predicted_outcome: an increase in the glass-forming ability by 20% relative to the baseline alloy without Y addition, as measured by the critical cooling rate required to form a fully amorphous structure
generation.boundary: the optimal Y addition range is between 1-2 at.%, beyond which the glass-forming ability may decrease due to the formation of Y-rich crystalline phases
generation.uncertainty: the exact mechanism of Y addition on glass formation is not fully understood and may depend on other factors such as cooling rate and alloy composition

falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: if the addition of 1-2 at.% Y to the Mg-based alloy does not result in an increase in glass-forming ability by at least 15% relative to the baseline alloy, the hypothesis is falsified
